(as Moores) | hq_location_city = [[Geelong]] | hq_location_country = [[Victoria, Australia]] }} '''Bright and Hitchcocks''' (also known as '''Brights''') was a [[department store]] in [[Geelong]], [[Victoria, Australia]], operating on the same site from 1855 to 1979. The building remains today on the south-east corner of Moorabool and Little Malop Streets in central [[Geelong central business district|Geelong]]. [[Image:Bright and hitchcocks - geelong, victoria - 2007.jpg|280px|thumb|The former store in 2007]] ==Beginnings== The business had its origins in 1850, after three brothers, G.M., William and W.M. Hitchcock, emigrated from [[London]] to Geelong with a cargo of merchandise and opened a store in Yarra Street. In 1853, William Bright, who had a shop in Moorabool Street, formed a partnership with G.M. and W.M. Hitchcock, and the new firm traded as Bright & Co. After Bright's retirement, the Hitchcock brothers continued to trade as Bright & Hitchcocks.{{cite web|title=Bright & Hitchcocks Pty. Ltd.|url=http://xena.lib.unimelb.edu.au/cgi-bin/library?form=Accessions-new-3.all&accessio_1=61&accessio_2=4|website=University of Melbourne Archives Database Search|accessdate=2017-04-09|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070613192918/http://xena.lib.unimelb.edu.au/cgi-bin/library?form=Accessions-new-3.all&accessio_1=61&accessio_2=4|archivedate=2007-06-13}} By 1926, when the company was sold to five of its senior employees, it was the largest department store in provincial Victoria. The son of one of the founding brothers, [[Howard Hitchcock]], was the last of the family to be involved with the store, retiring in 1927.{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article148715368 |title=Death of Mr G. M. Hitchcock. |newspaper=[[Geelong Advertiser]] |issue=20,299 |location=Victoria, Australia |date=8 May 1912 |accessdate=5 December 2018 |page=3 |via=National Library of Australia}} ==Changes== Bright and Hitchcocks became a public company in 1950 with almost 600 shareholders. In 1959, the company was purchased by Cox Brothers, which was a major Australian retailer, operating over 100 stores.{{cite web|title=Cox Brothers (Australia) Ltd (1928 - )|url=http://www.gabr.net.au/biogs/ABE0060b.htm|website=Guide to Australian Business Records|publisher=Archive Research Consultancy|accessdate=2017-04-09}} Cox Brothers ran into financial problems and went into receivership in 1966.{{cite Australian Dictionary of Biography |last1=Humphries|first1=Michael E.|title=Richardson, Sir Horace Frank (1901–1983)|id2=richardson-sir-horace-frank-14452|accessdate=2017-04-09}} In March 1968, the store was sold to new owners, who changed the name to "Brights", the name by which the store had been known for many years previously. It was sold again, in January 1969, to Sydney-based [[Burns Philp|Burns Philp & Company]], who renamed the store "Mates", as part of the company's [[Albury]], [[New South Wales]]-based department store chain. The final sale was in 1976 when Chas Moore took over the lease, changing the name again, this time to "Moores". [[Image:Bright and hitchcocks - geelong, victoria - 2006.jpg|thumb|The store before repainting in 2006]] ==Closure== Moores closed in 1979, and the building was divided into a number of smaller shops at the street level. The upper floors have since been empty, but the basement was occupied by a [[Spotlight Group|Spotlight]] fabric store until 2005. The exterior of the building underwent a repaint and minor refurbishment in 2006. Part of the ground floor is now a [[7-Eleven]] [[convenience store]]. ==Images== * [http://www.slv.vic.gov.au/pictoria/gid/slv-pic-aab72959 Bright & Hitchcock's Store 1900] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Further reading== * Peter Begg (1990).
